# Set Mismatch. The answer is [doubled, absent]: the integer counted twice
# first, then the one counted zero times.

@example n = 5: 5 appears twice and 2 not at all; 1, 3 and 4 appear once each.
[4,5,1,3,5]
=> [5,2]

@example The doubled integer comes first even when it is the smaller one: 1 is counted twice, and 5 zero times.
[7,1,6,2,4,1,3]
=> [1,5]

@example The absent integer can be n itself: here n = 4, 3 is counted twice and 4 not at all.
[3,1,3,2]
=> [3,4]

# n = 2, the smallest: both elements are equal.
[2,2]
=> [2,1]

# Sorted, with 1 absent: there is no hole inside the array.
[2,2,3,4,5]
=> [2,1]

# Sorted, with n absent: no hole inside the array either.
[1,2,3,4,5,6,6]
=> [6,7]

# 1 doubled and n absent, then n doubled and 1 absent.
[5,1,7,3,1,6,2,4]
=> [1,8]

[8,6,4,2,3,8,7,5]
=> [8,1]

# The doubled integer just below the absent one, then just above it.
[7,4,1,6,2,4,3]
=> [4,5]

[6,2,7,1,6,3,4]
=> [6,5]

# Decreasing order, with the two integers far apart.
[8,7,6,5,4,3,2,2,1]
=> [2,9]
